founded.what: The year the house was founded at Aÿ by the son of a Colombian diplomat, whose name it carries.

place: Aÿ, Vallée de la Marne, Champagne

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: it grows grapes, buys more from growers and makes the wine itself, and the Union des Maisons de Champagne lists it among the houses.

story: Ayala takes its name from its founder, the son of a Colombian diplomat, who married, by the usual account, a niece of the Vicomte de Mareuil and received the Château d'Aÿ, with vineyards in Aÿ and Mareuil-sur-Aÿ, through her. He founded the house at Aÿ in 1860. In 1865, by the house's own account, he launched a dry Champagne, at 21 grams of sugar a litre when the sweet wines then in fashion carried far more. The wines found a following in England, where the future King Edward VII (1841 to 1910) was among the customers, as the Union des Maisons de Champagne records. In 1911 the growers' riots that swept through Aÿ destroyed the premises; the house was rebuilt and at work again by 1913. A long, quiet stretch followed, and the house changed hands more than once. On 7 January 2005 the holding company of Bollinger, its neighbour in Aÿ, bought it. It has been run since as a house of its own, set apart from Bollinger by Chardonnay and stainless steel. Perle d'Ayala, created in 1995 and aged under natural cork, came through the change as the prestige cuvée, and Brut Nature, with no dosage at all, followed in 2007.

style.line: Chardonnay led, fresh and precise, with little dosage: the house traces its dry style to 1865 and makes its wines in small stainless steel vats rather than in oak.
style.grapes: Chardonnay leads every blend, from about half of Brut Majeur to about four fifths of Perle d'Ayala, with Pinot Noir and Meunier; Brut Majeur draws on about seventy crus across Champagne, by the house's count.
style.reserve: Brut Majeur carries reserve wines, at least two fifths of the blend by one of the house's own sheets.
style.vessels: Each cru, each grape and each year is vinified apart in about 120 small stainless steel vats; the pages read speak of no oak.
style.lees: About three years on its lees for Brut Majeur, by the house; eight years and more under cork for Perle d'Ayala.
style.dosage: Low: 6 grams a litre for Brut Majeur on the house's page and 7 on an older sheet, and none at all for Brut Nature.

nv.name: Brut Majeur
nv.note: The non vintage Brut a guest meets first: Chardonnay led, with Pinot Noir and Meunier from about seventy crus, aged about three years on its lees.

cuvee.name: Perle d'Ayala

first.what: The year the house created the cuvée and its bottle, by its own account; its leaflet counts the 1990 and 1993 among the vintages.

cuvee.rhythm: Always a vintage wine and never made every year: the house's leaflet counts the 2015 as the thirteenth, after 1990, 1993, 1995, 1997, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2005, 2006, 2012 and 2013.
cuvee.blend: Chardonnay, about four fifths, with Pinot Noir for the rest, as the house states for the 2013 and 2015 vintages.
cuvee.sites: Grand Cru villages only. For the 2015 vintage the house names Chouilly, Cramant, Oger and Le Mesnil-sur-Oger in the Côte des Blancs and Aÿ itself; other vintages draw on other Grand Cru villages, Verzy among them.
cuvee.making: The wines are made in the house's small stainless steel vats. The bottles then age in the Aÿ cellars under natural cork rather than the metal crown cap most Champagne rests under, are riddled on traditional oak racks and are disgorged by hand. The dosage is low: 6 grams a litre for the 2012 and 2013 vintages, and 5 for the 2015, which the house labels Extra Brut.
cuvee.lees: Over eight years in the cellar under natural cork, by the house; its importer for the United States says nine.
cuvee.bottle: The Perle bottle, a shape of its own, came with the cuvée's first edition in 1995, by the house's account, and became the model for the house's other bottles. The cork that closes it for its years in the cellar is the detail to tell.
cuvee.young: On release it shows toasted bread, hazelnut and candied orange peel over lemon zest, with dried flowers, a fine, slow bead and a dry, lightly bitter, saline finish.
cuvee.aged: It is released already mature, after eight years and more under cork: past the first impression, the house's and its importer's notes for the 2015 vintage run on to cocoa, gingerbread and mild tobacco. How long it keeps after release the house does not state.

forms.name: Perle d'Ayala Nature
forms.note: The same blend with no dosage at all, sold for some vintages of the 2000s, the 2005 among them.

cuvee.serve: 10 to 12 degrees Celsius, the house's own sheet for the 2012 vintage advising 12; no need to decant; a tulip shaped glass rather than a narrow flute.

also.name: Grande Cuvée

first.what: Its first vintage was not found: one merchant lists a 1993 vintage, as Grande Cuvée Millésimé.

also.note: The first of the two names the class sheet prints for Ayala. Grande Cuvée was a vintage wine the house sold before Perle d'Ayala became its prestige cuvée: one merchant lists a Grande Cuvée Millésimé 1993 and a wine app lists an Ayala Grande Cuvée Brut. The house's own pages do not list it, and its blend, its villages and the span of its vintages could not be sourced. Learn it as a name of the past, and Perle d'Ayala as the cuvée the house created in 1995.
also.line: Grande Cuvée is the older Ayala name on the class sheet, found as a 1993 vintage, and Perle d'Ayala the prestige cuvée created in 1995.

table.house45: Ayala is a house of Aÿ, founded in 1860 by the son of a Colombian diplomat who married into the Château d'Aÿ. Five years later, by its own account, it released a Champagne far drier than the fashion, and dryness has been its mark since. It burned in the riots of 1911, was rebuilt, and in January 2005 was bought by the family group of its neighbour Bollinger. The two share a village and little else. Where Bollinger is Pinot Noir and oak barrels, Ayala is Chardonnay and stainless steel: fresh, precise and dry. Brut Majeur is the wine most guests meet, and Perle d'Ayala is its prestige cuvée.
table.house10: Ayala is the Chardonnay led house of Aÿ, founded in 1860 and a sister of Bollinger from 2005: fresh, dry and precise.
table.cuvee45: Perle d'Ayala is the prestige cuvée of Ayala, a vintage Champagne created in 1995. It is about four fifths Chardonnay with Pinot Noir for the rest, all from Grand Cru villages such as Chouilly, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger and Aÿ. What sets it apart is the cork. Most Champagne ages under a metal crown cap, but this one rests eight years and more under natural cork, which lets it mature slowly. Every bottle is then cleared of its sediment by hand and finished very dry. Expect toasted bread, hazelnut and candied orange peel, with a fine, saline finish. I pour it in a tulip glass, a little warmer than most Champagne.
table.sale: If you like Champagne with some age and toast but no heaviness, Perle d'Ayala is the one: mostly Grand Cru Chardonnay, matured eight years and more under natural cork. May I bring a bottle for the table?
table.cuvee10: Perle d'Ayala is Ayala's vintage prestige cuvée: Grand Cru Chardonnay with a little Pinot Noir, aged eight years and more under natural cork.
table.cuvee20: Perle d'Ayala is the prestige cuvée of Ayala, the Chardonnay house of Aÿ, created in 1995 and made only as a vintage wine. It ages eight years and more under natural cork, so it arrives toasty and mature while staying dry and fresh.

guests.q: Is Ayala the same as Bollinger?
guests.a: No. They are neighbours in Aÿ, and Bollinger's family group bought Ayala in January 2005, but the wines are made apart and taste apart: Ayala is Chardonnay led and made in steel, Bollinger Pinot Noir led and made in oak.

During its years in the cellar a natural cork lets in a trace more air than a metal crown cap, so the wine matures slowly and gains toast and hazelnut; the house credits the cork for the wine's depth.
No. The 2012, 2013 and 2015 vintages were finished with five or six grams of sugar a litre, the 2015 labelled Extra Brut, which is drier than most Brut Champagne.

traps: The class sheet prints two names for Ayala: Grand Cuvée, which is the older vintage wine Grande Cuvée, and Perle d'Ayala, the prestige cuvée created in 1995.
Grande Cuvée alone means Krug to most guests and examiners: asked for the prestige cuvée of Ayala, answer Perle d'Ayala.
Bollinger's group bought Ayala in 2005, yet Ayala is no second label of Bollinger: its style is Chardonnay and steel, not Pinot Noir and oak.
The house has headed the cuvée Perle d'Ayala, La Perle and Perle by vintage: all three are the one wine.

sheet.label: Grande Cuvée; Perle d'Ayala
sheet.note: The sheet drops the e of Grande and prints the older wine first. Perle d'Ayala is the prestige cuvée; the house's own sheets head the 2012 and 2013 vintages La Perle and the 2015 Perle, and its American importer lists the 2015 as Cuvée Perle d'Ayala.

cards.front: Ayala: name its prestige cuvée and the year of its first vintage.
cards.back: Perle d'Ayala, created by the house in 1995, though its own leaflet counts 1990 and 1993 among its vintages. The class sheet also prints the older Grande Cuvée.

cards.front: Perle d'Ayala: which house makes it, and in which village?
cards.back: Ayala, of Aÿ, bought by Bollinger's family group in January 2005.

cards.front: Under what closure does Perle d'Ayala age, and for how long?
cards.back: Natural cork rather than a crown cap, for eight years and more; it is then disgorged by hand.

questions.q: A guest asks for the prestige cuvée of Bollinger's sister house in Aÿ. Which wine do you bring?
questions.exp: Ayala, bought by Bollinger's group in January 2005, makes Perle d'Ayala. La Grande Année is Bollinger's own vintage wine, Amour de Deutz comes from Deutz, also of Aÿ, and Clos des Goisses from Philipponnat.

questions.q: By the house's own account, what set Ayala's Champagne of the 1865 vintage apart from the wines of its day?
opts: It was far drier than the fashion
It was the first rosé made by blending
It came from a single walled vineyard
It was fermented entirely in new oak
questions.exp: The house dates its dry style to the 1865 vintage, a low dosage wine at a time when Champagne was sweet. The first known blended rosé is credited to Veuve Clicquot, and the single walled vineyard is Philipponnat's Clos des Goisses.

questions.q: Which closure does Perle d'Ayala age under in the cellar, where most Champagne does not?
questions.exp: Perle d'Ayala rests eight years and more under natural cork, which lets it mature slowly. Most Champagne ages under a crown cap and meets its cork only after it has been disgorged.

report: Ayala is not in the library, so every fact rests on the house's own pages, the Union des Maisons de Champagne or two secondary sources.

kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label. The Union des Maisons de Champagne lists Maison Ayala among the houses, and a house that buys grapes beyond its own vines is a négociant manipulant by the definition of the French consumer authority; a refuter should read a label.
The founder's dates were not found in two sources, so he is described and never named apart from the house.

Left out for want of a second source or because sources disagree: the Syndicat des Grandes Marques of 1882 (Wikipedia alone), the year the Frey group bought the house (1995 by two accounts, 2000 by memory) and the owners of the middle of the twentieth century; the 21 grams of the 1865 wine are the house's own figure.

Grande Cuvée, the sheet's first name: only two listings were found, a merchant's Grande Cuvée Millésimé 1993 and a wine app's Ayala Grande Cuvée Brut, so its blend, its villages and its span of vintages are left out and also.first.year is empty. The plan's standing of before rests on that 1993; the Groupe Bollinger leaflet for Perle 2015 also counts a 1993 among Perle's twelve earlier vintages, so how the two names stand is left open by the refuter.

The label's name: merchants' labels of the 2002, 2005 and 2006 vintages read Perle d'Ayala, the house's own sheets head 2012 and 2013 La Perle and the 2015 Perle, and Vintus lists the 2015 as Cuvée Perle d'Ayala.

Malolactic conversion is not stated on the pages read, so style.malolactic is empty; whether the Perle wines see only steel is the house's general statement of its vats and not a statement of the cuvée's own sheet.
Time under cork: over eight years by the house, nine by the importer; the record says eight years and more.

The Brut Majeur blend moved between the house's sheets (45 to 55 per cent Chardonnay, dosage 7 then 6 grams a litre, a minimum of 40 per cent reserve wines on one sheet), so the record gives it in words.
The cork letting in a trace more air than a crown cap is the Groupe Bollinger leaflet for Perle 2015, which speaks of slow micro-oxygenation; the refuter added the leaflet to the sources.

The young glass draws on the house's notes for the 2013 and 2015 vintages and a critic's note on the 2012; the aged glass on the deeper notes the house and the importer give for the 2015. No note of a bottle kept long after release was found, and the record does not invent one.

changed: cuvee.first, story, rhythm, bottle, also, the table lines, traps[0] and cards[0].back: 1995 is the year the house created the cuvée and its bottle, not certainly its first vintage; the Groupe Bollinger leaflet for Perle 2015 counts the 2015 as the thirteenth vintage after 1990, 1993, 1995, 1997, 1999, 2000, 2001, 2002, 2005, 2006, 2012 and 2013, and marks thirty years of the cuvée.
cuvee.rhythm: the thirteenth vintage is no longer said to be counted since 1995, a count the house's list does not make; the twelve earlier vintages are named from the leaflet.

story: the 1865 wine is the house's dry Champagne at 21 grams of sugar a litre, by its heritage page; the house's calling it the first dry Champagne was not found and is cut; the marriage into the Château d'Aÿ is told as the usual account, since one merchant's story differs.
cuvee.serve: the house's 12 degrees is its sheet for the 2012 vintage, not the 2013.
cuvee.bottle: the Perle shape became the model for the house's other bottles, by the house.
style.vessels: no oak on the pages read, not a claim of every page of the house.
sale and cuvee10: eight years and more under cork, as the house gives at least eight.
sources: the heritage page, the Groupe Bollinger leaflet and the world heritage mission's history page in place of the Brut Nature page, Wikipedia and the merchant's blog.
open: Perle d'Ayala's first vintage: the house created the cuvée and its bottle in 1995, while its own leaflet lists the 1990 and 1993 among its vintages; whether those two were first sold as Perle or under another name, Grande Cuvée perhaps, was not found.
How Grande Cuvée stands to Perle d'Ayala: a 1993 is listed under both names, so the plan's standing of before is not settled.
NM was not read on a label; it rests on the Union des Maisons de Champagne listing the house and on the definition.
Malolactic conversion: not stated on any page read.
